recipes.name: Traditional Layered French Croissants
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups unsalted butter, at room temperature

steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of flour over the butter and mix it together with your hands in a mixing bowl or on a work surface. Transfer the butter to a length of foil or parchment paper and pat it into a 6 inch square. Fold up the foil to make a packet and refrigerate until chilled, about 2 hours.

Combine 2 cups of the flour with the salt and sugar in a mixing bowl. Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm water (100 degrees F/38 degrees C) and set aside until frothy, about 10 minutes. Meanwhile, warm the milk and the heavy cream to lukewarm. Add the yeast, milk, and cream to the flour mixture and stir well. The dough will have a batter-like consistency.

Stir in the remaining 2 cups of flour 1/4 cup at a time to form a soft dough. It should no longer be sticky. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured work surface and knead until smooth, about 5 minutes. Place the dough in a mixing bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 1 hour.

To begin the rolling and folding process, both the butter and the dough should be at a cool room temperature. [See Cook's Note.] Place the dough on a floured surface and roll it into a 10-inch square. Set the block of butter diagonally on the square dough. Bring each point of dough to the center of the butter square; the edges of the dough should overlap. Pinch the edges together to seal.

Starting from the center of the square and working outward, use a rolling pin to roll the dough out into a rectangle. The butter should be pliable enough to roll smoothly with the dough; if it's too soft and starts to ooze out the corners, wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate before proceeding. Roll the dough into a long rectangle, approximately 8 by 18 inches. Fold the length of dough into thirds, like a business letter.

If the dough is still cool, you can continue with another fold. Otherwise, wrap it in plastic and refrigerate for 45 minutes to 1 hour. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and let it warm up for about 10 minutes before you begin rolling it out again.

Position the dough so that the open ends are at 12 and 6 o'clock. Roll the dough into a rectangle, working from the center of the dough and pressing outwards. Reposition the dough as necessary to fit your work space. You should have a long rectangle for the "book fold." Fold both ends of the dough into the middle; the ends don't have to be touching, but should be close. Fold the already-folded dough in half; it will look like a thick book. Wrap the dough well with plastic and refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours.

Remove the dough from the refrigerator and let it rest at room temperature for about 20 minutes. Roll the dough into a rectangle again and fold it into thirds, like a business letter. Wrap it in plastic and refrigerate for 4-6 hours or overnight.

To shape the croissants, roll the dough into a 10- by 38-inch rectangle on a lightly floured work surface. It should be about 1/4 inch thick. Use a pizza wheel or sharp paring knife to trim the edges of the dough. Divide the rectangle in half so that you have two 5-inch wide strips of dough. Use a clean yardstick to mark each strip into triangles that are 5 inches wide at their bases. Cut the triangles and place them onto parchment-lined baking sheets. Chill for 15 to 20 minutes, if necessary.

Starting at the base of the triangle, roll the dough up into a log; the tip of the triangle should be under the body of the croissant to prevent it from unraveling. Bend in the corners to form the traditional crescent shape. Repeat with the remaining dough.
Arrange the croissants on the parchment-lined baking sheets and allow to rise until doubled in size, about 1 to 2 hours.

Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash. Brush the croissants with egg wash and bake in the preheated oven until deep brown, 22 to 25 minutes. Cool on a rack before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Traditional Layered French Croissants
raw_recipe.description: This classic laminated croissant dough takes time and effort, but if you're feeling ambitious, you can make authentic melt-in-your-mouth pastries!

review.reviewBody: I love these. This recipe is also very detailed, so it's easy to follow. One problem was the cooking time. I found it took only 13-15 or so minutes. Not the 22-25 minutes in the recipe.

Everything in this recipe seems to be spot on...except the bake time. 425 degrees at 22 minutes (minimum time given) is way too long. I over baked half of my recipe (and work) by following this time. The second pan I am giving 16 minutes and then watching. This is not an oven to oven temperature difference...it's a frustrating bake time error in the recipe.

I was a baker at a French style bakery for 10 years. That was 20 years ago. I made many a croissant in my day, but only in my small commercial bakery, and only in large batches. I’ve never attempted home made croissants until now. 

Tip 1) follow the instructions. Don't try to rush. The colder the dough, the easier the rolling

The instructions were solid. I also had the benefit of a rolling pin I can fill with water and freeze. Really makes the roll out process easier. If things get too warm, the butter melts and rolling becomes impossible. If you notice your dough softening, stop, wrap, refrigerate. Easy peasy. 

I made chocolate almond croissant with almond paste I made from another recipe on this site. I added a slice of paste, about 2 tbs Choc chips and rolled then up. Then I dusted with icing sugar and drizzled with melted chocolate.

Huge hit. Next I'm trying Apple turnovers using the same dough.

First time pastry maker here and it was a success! I can't get over how great they turned out. This was only my 2nd time ever baking from scratch so I needed the detailed instructions. Yes, this is very time consuming but well worth it. I got RAVE reviews and some thought these were professionally made. I'm not kidding! 
Few things I did differently: 
- used salted butter (next time I'm going try using salted European sweet cream butter)
- instead of heavy cream I opted for sweetend condensed milk (which eliminated the need to add sugar)
-added some warm water to help the dough mix better (I'm at 7,600 ft elevation)
- double basted the croissants with the egg wash
- added dark chocolate chips to half the batch
- adjusted the baking temperature to 385 for 20 minutes. I think times and temperature will vary based on your oven and elevation. 

I was looking to make something by hand and don't have a mixer. I found these to be very tasty, rewarding and I can't wait to try them again!

I loved these. I didn't give it 5 stars because I added a tsp of salt to the unsalted butter per other reviews. I also thought that making the block of butter 6 inch square was too thick for the initial roll and it did not spread into the first layer of dough consistently. I went online and watched another how to video on croissants and followed those directions. I proofed in the fridge overnight. The bake time for me was 375º F for 15 minutes rotate the pans and then 10-15 minutes longer. A word of caution. After shaping them watch the final proof and don't let it go too long. The second batch went a tad too long setting on the stove while the first baked and were a bit flat - delicious though. I put the last 2 trays of formed croissants back in the fridge while the second of 3 batches baked and they were perfect.

I did not change anything the first time I made these. And they were utterly buttery, crispy on the outside and about a zillion soft layers in the inside. Just perfect. I could go on and on raving about these. I cooked them for exactly 17 minutes, half the time on one side, then turned them over and they were perfectly golden brown. Right now, as I type, I've started the croissant dough process again, only, this time, using half All Purpose Flour and half Whole Wheat Flour. Will update eventually how they turn up, although I'm perfectly confident they will be the delicious, buttery, crispy and yet soft layered treats that everybody would be dying to devour! Thank you so very very much for the detailed instructions.

Thanks so much for a great, detailed recipe! It was my first attempt at any real pastry and it was a huge success! This isn't difficult at all if you have patience. I spread a little bit of almond paste on some of them before rolling and sprinkled sliced almonds on top after brushing on the egg wash to make my favorite french treat, croissant aux amandes!

This is an excellent recipe. However, 1/2 teaspoon of salt is simply not enough. Next time I make it I will simply use salted butter. Also, I baked for 10 minutes at 400 then turned the trays around and baked for an additional 12 minutes at 350.

As other reviewers have noted, the baking times and temperature are vastly off. I baked at 375 deg F for about 15 minutes. Your mileage may vary based on the size of the dough. Having said that, the croissants turned out beautifully. Buttery and flaky and just fantastic. The recipe is incredibly detailed you can't possibly go wrong. Be patient and take your time. In the time it takes to make these things from scratch you could hop in an airplane, fly to Paris, pick up a dozen, and fly home.

I changed them to use half cake flour and next time I will use 1/3-1/2 salted butter instead of all unsalted. Rise at cooler room temp (sub 80 F) or your butter will melt and soak into your pastry, making it tough.

I thought the recipe made this too complicated - it did not take me so many chill/thaw times. The croissants look nice on the outside, but the inside was not completely done. They also lacked flavor like others mentioned. Next time, I will add more salt and bake them at a lower temperature.
it was really buttery and flaky. but it tasted a lot like biscuits, which i could have made with a lot less time and effort. so not worth it.
it took a wee while to make but totally worth it. They are just so good, flaky and soft, really something - I'll be putting my own recipe to one side replacing it with this one. Thanks for sharing
good but temperate was too high, don't go stale quickly
Mine were a bit thin. But other than that I loved it.

This absolutely tastes authentic. I'm from Belgium so I know what's up ;) I've made these for a bake sale and they went within 30 min. The 20 hours I put in was worth it though! Love this dish. Although a little time consuming absolutely worth it.
These turn out fluffy and buttery and just amazing!! I have made them 4 or 5 times now and they are always great!
This is a great recipe. I had to prepare it in a rush (one of those life or death situations), so I cheated by cooling in the freezer, but yet the results were really good.
The directions were easy to follow, but took forever to make! The result tastes like heaven, totally worth it.
Amazing recipe. Thank you for taking the time to write out the instructions. Followed the instructions step by step and ended up with the best croissants, all that was missing was the Champs-Elysees.
